record.title: BUBR1 Insufficiency in Mice Increases Their Sensitivity to Oxidative Stress
record.metadata_basis: Parent draft plus same-title institutional thesis source; no new remote metadata retrieval.

root_declaration.attribution: Parent/root declaration in bromate-qualification.md and retrieval.json, preserved without claiming independent reproduction.

independent_reviewer.scope: Read parent draft and saved retrieval record; read complete saved institutional thesis abstract text, visually checked PDF content page 2 and figure page 3; inspected institutional metadata context. Main-paper details absent from the thesis remain attributed to root.

model.root_reported_baseline: Lacks overt progeria under baseline conditions
model.independent_model_limit: The 20% value and baseline phenotype are not independently confirmed from the saved thesis abstract. This model must not be equated with a particular patient's variants or all BubR1 hypomorphs.

challenge.role: Experimental oxidative stressor; no therapeutic intervention
challenge.dose_provenance: Institutional thesis abstract Methods, independently read and visually checked. Nominal drinking-water concentration is not an administered mg/kg dose or human exposure equivalent.

outcomes.death_count_provenance: Parent's main-text reading; thesis survival graph corroborates direction and flat untreated curves, not independently resolved event/group counts.

outcomes.independent_thesis_support: Among animals completing treatment, the low-BubR1 group showed gastrointestinal bleeding and splenic lesions occupied by highly proliferative Ki-67-positive non-B/non-T-like cells; listed negative markers include CD3 and CD45R.
outcomes.count_provenance: Number two is from parent main-text reading; thesis summary does not supply that count.
outcomes.inference_limit: Suggestive neoplastic pathology in survivors does not prove cancer caused earlier deaths. Dehydration/hemorrhage explanations and absent explanatory gross lesions in early deaths are root-attributed body details.

outcomes.root_reported_result: Bromate reduces proliferation more strongly in low-BubR1 cells, with lower baseline proliferation already present.

concentration_conflict.basis: Parent's article-text reading; no native journal figure/PDF or raw culture data available locally.

outcomes.root_reported_result: Both bromate-treated genotypes lost weight; no significant between-genotype difference.
Increased with bromate; no significant difference between the two treated genotypes.
outcomes.inference_limit: A nonsignificant difference is not proof of equal exposure or tissue damage.

outcomes.independent_thesis_support: BUN is higher in treated low-BubR1 mice versus untreated and treated wild-type comparators; thesis reports p<0.05.
root_reported_nulls: No stated treatment-related increase in creatinine
No stated treatment-related increase in AST
No stated treatment-related increase in ALT
outcomes.inference_limit: Survivor measurements do not establish physiology or cause of death in animals that died earlier.

unresolved_items: Starting/analysis group denominators across article Results and survival caption
Native journal figure/PDF and raw-data verification absent
Maintext details not reproduced by independent reviewer

interpretation.supported: Oxidative-challenge vulnerability in a low-BubR1 mouse model; useful adverse context for assay endpoint selection.
not_established: Benefit of any antioxidant, including niacin, NAC or ascorbate
Variant-specific redox mechanism or therapy for a patient's BUB1B genotype
Cancer as demonstrated cause of the earlier deaths
Equal genotype exposure/damage from nonsignificant 8-OHdG comparison
interpretation.nomination: Decline therapeutic nomination; do not upgrade drug ranking.
interpretation.endpoint_implication: Preserve absolute survival, proliferation and lesion burden when interpreting apparent cell selection.

independent_draft_check.recommended_small_addition: The independently read thesis confirms 2 g/L KBrO3 in drinking water for 16 weeks; optional to include this nominal challenge dose in the Markdown.
independent_draft_check.extraction_note: Saved thesis text has an H/H-looking legend artifact; the actual page-3 figure labels the treated low-expression group L/L. Do not create an extra H/H group.
